memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses said, 'You have been set apart to the Lord today, for you were against your own sons and brothers, and he has blessed you this day.'" - Exod 32:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Levites' obedience cost them something deeply personal. They acted against their own families. And out of that day came their setting apart for God's service.

We should be careful how we apply this. This was a specific historical calling for one tribe at one moment. God is not asking us to take up swords against our relatives.

But there is a principle Jesus Himself carried forward with startling clarity: anyone who loves father or mother more than Him is not worthy of Him (Matt 10:37). Loyalty to Christ sometimes cuts across our closest relationships. Many believers know this painfully — a family that does not understand, a parent who feels betrayed, a spouse who resents the change.

If that is you, take heart. Jesus never pretended following Him would be free of cost. But He also promised that no one who has left family for His sake will fail to receive a hundredfold, and a family in Him (Mark 10:29-30).

Being "set apart" always involves separation from something. Yet what we are set apart *to* is far greater than what we are set apart *from*. In Christ, we are a chosen people, a royal priesthood (1 Pet 2:9) — not by tribe, but by grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has following Christ cost you in your relationships?
2. Where is your loyalty to Jesus being tested right now?
3. Do you see yourself as set apart for God's purposes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are worth every cost. Strengthen me where following You is hardest. Amen.
